study type: Qualitative analysis of intervention sessions from a randomized controlled trial
exposure: manualized speech and language intervention (Social Communication Intervention Programme - SCIP)
Metacognition in therapy content and delivery
outcome: Presence and themes of metacognition in therapy
Children's ability to monitor language, pragmatic and social interaction skills
cohort: A purposive sample of eight filmed therapy sessions from five children (aged 5;11 to 10;3) participating in the SCIP trial, who have social (pragmatic) communication disorder (SPCD).
finding: Thematic analysis revealed the presence of metacognition in the content and delivery of SCIP intervention, identifying four main themes: metacognitive person, task and strategy knowledge, and monitoring/control, which contribute to developing children's self-monitoring abilities.
